indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the chosen letters are read from right to left
the leading letters of the word Rastafarian, its front four, are taken

explanation.surface: A Rastafarian movement's leaders throw their support behind an old emperor, perhaps Haile Selassie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks like support, but it turns RAST, the first four letters of Rastafarian, round.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of the Russian monarchs, whose empire ended in 1917, so a ruler of the past.

clue.text: That woman has two articles to enclose

parts.note: the pronoun for a woman just mentioned is she
the indefinite article a and the definite article the

explanation.surface: A grammar note: some woman has a pair of articles to put in an envelope.
explanation.definitionFit: To put a blade in its scabbard, or more widely to cover or encase something.

clue.text: Part of helicopter going up and down

definitions.note: the spinning blade assembly on top of a helicopter is one of its parts

indicators.note: in a down clue the word reads the same going up the grid as coming down it

parts.note: the spinning blade assembly on top of a helicopter is one of its parts

explanation.surface: A helicopter's part that rises and descends, as helicopters do.
explanation.definitionFit: The rotating assembly of blades that lifts a helicopter is its main spinning component.

clue.text: Musician rings any number to get mother admitted

indicators.note: admitted means let inside, so mother goes into the other letters

parts.note: bands are rings, as in wedding bands
N stands for an unspecified number in algebra
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A musician telephones random numbers so that his mother can be let in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rings' looks like phoning, but it means bands.
explanation.definitionFit: A player in a brass or military band is a kind of performer of music.

definitions.meaning: a long fluffy feather wrap worn round the neck
a large constricting serpent of tropical America

explanation.surface: A scarf that is named after a snake.
explanation.definitionFit: The feather stole is named after the constrictor it resembles when draped round the neck.

clue.text: Really expressing agreement about King and I

indicators.note: about means around, so the agreeing word wraps the other letters

parts.note: nodding the head shows that one agrees
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Someone sincerely agrees about the musical The King and I.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The King and I' is a Rodgers and Hammerstein musical, which the surface leans on.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation 'Really?' and the phrase both express surprise or insist on truth, an idiom.

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for united inside the word for launches

parts.note: launches as a noun means beginnings or starts
U is a common abbreviation for united, as in football club names

explanation.surface: A royal family stays together during ship launches.
explanation.definitionFit: The dynasty that ruled Scotland and later England, from James I to Queen Anne.

indicators.note: missing first means the opening letter of the word for vote is dropped

parts.note: a ballot is a vote

explanation.surface: Someone missed the first vote on a grant of funds.
explanation.definitionFit: To grant something is to assign or apportion it as a share, a synonym.

clue.text: What retired teller did in Parisian milieu?

definitions.meaning: a bank cashier, or teller, who retired departed from the bank
the south bank of the Seine in Paris, the artistic and student quarter

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the answer as a verb and a noun: departed the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rive Gauche is the Paris district famous for artists, writers and cafes.

indicators.note: extremely means taking the extremes, the first and last letters, of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A list of adjectives for something lumpy and plain, heaping on dislike.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a string of synonyms, but only the last word is the definition; 'extremely' looks like an intensifier.
explanation.definitionFit: An unpleasant situation, mood or scene is described as nasty or threatening, the same sense.
The noun is slang for jail and also means a disturbance or commotion, two separate senses.

clue.text: Stubborn old boy expected to hold rodent

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: to hold means the word for expected contains the rodent

parts.note: something due is expected
a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: A former pupil who is expected to look after a pet rat is being obstinate.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstinately refusing to change one's mind, a straightforward synonym.

indicators.note: represented means presented again in another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The White Rose emblem of Yorkshire is shown in another way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Represented' looks like depicted, but here it reads re-presented: the letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaning in another way or in a different manner, a direct synonym.

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters are scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone passes beneath the broken arches of an old building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go through' looks like walking under the arches, but means examine.
explanation.definitionFit: To look through something thoroughly, such as a drawer or pockets, is to hunt in it.

clue.text: Stagger away, say, without apparent effort

parts.note: to reel is to stagger
off means away, as in going off

explanation.surface: Someone totters off, apparently with no trouble at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like the 'for example' marker, but belongs to the definition as the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To recite a list quickly and fluently, as if effortlessly, is this phrasal verb.

clue.text: Praying mantis, say, as part of religious group?

parts.note: in means as part of, as in being in a team
a sect is a religious group

explanation.surface: Is a praying mantis a member of some religious group, given its pious pose?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Praying' suggests religion, but a praying mantis is just an example of a bug.
explanation.definitionFit: The mantis is an example of a six-legged creature; 'say' marks it as one instance.

indicators.note: we hear means the clue is spoken, so a word that sounds alike is entered

parts.note: chard is a leafy vegetable, as in Swiss chard

explanation.surface: A vegetable that, we are told, has been burned.
explanation.definitionFit: Burned and blackened on the surface, a synonym.

indicators.note: stumbling means tripping up, so the letters fall into another order

explanation.surface: A high jumper regrets stumbling during the event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High jumper' suggests an athlete; it is an amphibian that leaps among branches.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbing amphibian that lives and leaps among the branches, described playfully.

explanation.surface: An English river of just the right height.
explanation.definitionFit: The major European waterway flowing through Switzerland, Germany and the Netherlands.

definitions.meaning: a term of endearment, like darling

explanation.definitionFit: The word means costly and is also an affectionate address like sweetheart.

clue.text: Row before editor had a meal

indicators.note: before puts the word for row ahead of the editor

parts.note: a din is a row, a noisy racket

explanation.surface: An argument before the editor sat down to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel (rhymes with now), and that sense of noise is the one used.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat dinner, a formal synonym for eating a meal.

clue.text: A bit of fluff in one's sherry

indicators.note: a bit of means part of, so the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A speck of fluff has fallen into someone's glass of sherry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link, but its letters are part of the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: A light, dry Spanish sherry from Jerez, an example of the drink.

parts.note: an infant is a young child
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
Y is a mathematical unknown, like x

explanation.surface: A child dashes off with unknown soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs' looks like a verb, but it is the cricket scorecard R.
explanation.definitionFit: Foot soldiers as a body, the army's fighting troops on foot.

clue.text: Suitable starters for feast in trattoria

indicators.note: starters means the first letters of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Appropriate first courses for a meal in an Italian restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starters' looks like antipasti, but it means initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Fit for purpose, appropriate, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Most verdant meadow seen before short holiday abroad

indicators.note: seen before puts the meadow ahead of the shortened holiday

parts.note: a lea is a meadow, a poetic word

indicators.note: short means the last letter of the word for a holiday abroad is cut off

parts.note: a fiesta is a holiday in Spain

explanation.surface: The greenest meadow is spotted ahead of a short trip abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdant means green with foliage, so the most verdant has the most foliage.

indicators.note: before puts the useless item ahead of the chosen letter

parts.note: a dud is something useless

indicators.note: 4th of picks the fourth letter of the word November

explanation.surface: A Guy Fawkes effigy is useless before Bonfire Night, which falls on the 5th of November.
explanation.walkthrough: Guy Fawkes, burned in effigy on 5 November in Britain, misleads: 'Guy' just means man.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for a man or fellow, synonyms in casual speech.
